solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awful singer to pack it in

indicators.note: an awful version of the word singer is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful vocalist is being told to give up singing for good.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack it in is to quit or give up, which is what someone who stands down from a post does.

clue.text: Girl and American pal making bloomer

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
bud is American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A girl and her US friend make an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it means something that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is a rose not yet open, a flower that is about to bloom.

clue.text: Go away from academic room in the morning

parts.note: SCR is the senior common room of a college
AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the college common room early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Live with a girl almost out of control? See if that works!

indicators.note: out of control signals that the gathered letters run wild into a new order
almost means the word girl stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Moving in with a wild girl is an experiment worth trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GIRL to GIR; 'out of control' rearranges LIVEWITHAGIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a whirl is an idiom for trying it out to find whether it succeeds.

clue.text: Change hands after turning around

indicators.note: turning around signals that the word for hands is read backwards

parts.note: paws is an informal word for hands

explanation.surface: Something passes from one person's hands to another's after they turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: To change one thing for another is to exchange or trade them.

clue.text: Wife and I rowed terribly? My wife's now gone

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of rowed are muddled

explanation.surface: A husband and wife quarrelled badly, and now she has left him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowed' rhymes with 'loud' here (quarrelled), not with 'road'; 'terribly' rearranges ROWED into DOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A widower is a man whose spouse has died, which is how he might put it himself.

clue.text: Quietly put on attire for exploration

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a robe is a garment, a form of attire

explanation.surface: Someone slips on clothing quietly before setting out to explore.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough investigation, a kind of exploration of a matter.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about learner showing mirth

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the other letter

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A surprised cry about a novice driver causes laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is delight or merriment, a synonym of mirth.

clue.text: Hurry to obtain caustic extract from newspaper

parts.note: to press is to urge on or hurry
a cutting remark is caustic or wounding

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to get a scathing piece out of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an article clipped out of a newspaper.

clue.text: Lose vitality being awfully liverish when one passes out

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of liverish are thrown into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone feeling very liverish loses their energy and faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one passes out' removes an I from LIVERISH; 'awfully' rearranges what is left (LVERISH).
explanation.definitionFit: Something that shrivels wilts and dries up, losing its freshness and life.

clue.text: Artist and fashion designer not finishing off set

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist

indicators.note: not finishing off means the designer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: An artist and a couturier fail to complete a stage or film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing off' drops the last R of DIOR, leaving DIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio set is the receiving apparatus, so 'set' is a short name for the device.

clue.text: Layabouts sitting around trees — quality of uncomfortable ground?

indicators.note: sitting around means the idlers' word is placed round the trees

parts.note: bums is slang for idlers or layabouts
pines are evergreen trees

explanation.surface: Idlers lounge among trees, and the uneven earth is uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven, lumpy terrain has bumps, so its bumpy nature is the quality described.

clue.text: You and I possessing nothing — misery

indicators.note: possessing means the pronoun holds the zero inside it

parts.note: you and I together are we
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A couple who own nothing are wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is great sorrow or distress, a synonym of misery.

clue.text: Unhappy about housing everyone in US city

indicators.note: housing means the reversed word encloses the other piece
about signals that the word for unhappy turns round

parts.note: unhappy means sad
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable about providing homes for all the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Part of a flight or the end of one?

definitions.meaning: the level area between flights of stairs
an aircraft's ... is the end of a journey by air

explanation.surface: A question about where a staircase or a journey stops.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stair platform and an aircraft coming down to earth.

clue.text: Son was worried, frightened

parts.note: cared can mean was concerned or worried

explanation.surface: A boy was anxious and afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and frightened are synonyms, both meaning afraid.

clue.text: One falsely imprisoned doctor you upset — endless commotion

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for you upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fuss means a commotion

explanation.surface: A doctor is upset by an endless fuss over a wrongful jailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns YE to EY; 'endless' cuts FUSS to FUS. Alfred Dreyfus was a French officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreyfus was jailed on Devil's Island for treason he did not commit, the classic wrongful imprisonment.

clue.text: Fellow from east side of capital city

indicators.note: east side of means only the right-hand end of the city's name is kept, as on a map

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: A man comes from the East End of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer the east side is the right-hand end, so LONDON keeps its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, and a fellow is a senior member of a college.

clue.text: Dorothy keeps record in storehouse

indicators.note: keeps means the name holds the record inside it

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman stores a record in her warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a place where goods are stored, a warehouse.

clue.text: School finally not able to provide dining facility for its staff?

parts.note: high is short for high school

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A school finds itself unable to give its teachers a place to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: High table is the raised table in a college hall where the fellows and senior staff dine.

clue.text: My journey ends with request for silence

indicators.note: ends with means the first piece is followed by the second

parts.note: a go can mean a trip or journey, as in to go somewhere
sh is said to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone's trip finishes with a call for hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not possessive here but the exclamation, as in 'My, that's big!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: Beer and suchlike? You may hear shouts of disapproval

indicators.note: you may hear means the word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: boos are shouts of disapproval

explanation.surface: Drinkers might hear jeers about beer and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink, of which beer is an example.

clue.text: Earlier head of religious order

definitions.meaning: the superior of a priory or a deputy to an abbot

explanation.surface: Formerly the leader of a monastic community.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both as an adjective for previous and as a title for a monastery's superior.

clue.text: Escape quietly with undergarment removed

parts.note: a slip is a woman's undergarment
off can mean taken away or removed

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away after taking off their underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip off is to leave unobtrusively, an idiom for a quiet getaway.

clue.text: Clothes from stores ultimately got sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the combined letters are read in reverse
ultimately picks the final letter of stores

explanation.surface: Garments from a shop were eventually returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S; with GOT that is SGOT, and 'sent back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is an informal word for clothes or garments.

clue.text: Odd trees containing good birds

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the other piece
odd trees are strange ones, so the letters of trees are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some strange trees have fine birds nesting in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges TREES to ERETS, and 'containing' puts G in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, examples of wading birds.
